backlog.title: Bug Fix Remediation — pi-mulligan BUG-001 through BUG-006
backlog.description: Fix six verified bugs in the pi-mulligan extension: one Major (checkpoint consumption clearing wrong target on duplicate labels) and five Minor (config integer validation gaps, empty-needle resolver match, audit disabled-state inconsistency, and nuclear-rewind persisting no-op markers). All bugs are in edge cases not covered by the existing 949-test suite. The fixes are surgical, following established patterns (the maxRetriesPerPrompt integer-guard precedent, the tool-layer refusal convention, and defense-in-depth in the pure resolver tier).

milestones.title: Config Integer Validation Fixes (BUG-002, BUG-003)
milestones.description: Fix three integer-valued config knobs in src/config.ts validateConfig that accept fractional values: driftWindowTurns floors to 0 without a >= 1 guard (BUG-002), and shrink.maxActive/staleAfterFires accept fractions like 0.5 verbatim without flooring (BUG-003). All three follow the exact same pattern already established for rewind.maxRetriesPerPrompt: Number.isFinite(n) && Math.floor(n) >= 1 ? Math.floor(n) : default.

tasks.title: Fix driftWindowTurns integer validation (BUG-002)
tasks.description: Add the missing Math.floor(n) >= 1 guard to the nudges.driftWindowTurns branch of validateConfig so that a fractional value like 0.5 — which passes coerceNumber's > 0 check but floors to 0 — falls back to the default instead of producing a degenerate zero-length drift window.

subtasks.title: Add Math.floor >= 1 guard to driftWindowTurns in validateConfig

tasks.title: Fix shrink.maxActive and shrink.staleAfterFires integer validation (BUG-003)
tasks.description: Add Math.floor + >= 1 integer guards to shrink.maxActive and shrink.staleAfterFires in validateConfig so fractional values like 0.5 are rejected (falling back to defaults) instead of being accepted verbatim and silently neutering the shrink retirement subsystem.

subtasks.title: Add Math.floor >= 1 guards to maxActive and staleAfterFires in validateConfig

milestones.title: Pure Transform Defense-in-Depth (BUG-004)
milestones.description: Add an empty-needle guard to resolveShrinkTarget's by_content_includes arm in src/transforms.ts so that an empty string does not degenerately match the first message. This is defense-in-depth — the shrink tool layer already refuses empty discriminators, but the filter-level resolver should be self-protecting for old/persisted markers or hand-crafted entries that bypass tool validation.

tasks.title: Add empty-needle guard to resolveShrinkTarget by_content_includes arm
tasks.description: In src/transforms.ts, resolveShrinkTarget's by_content_includes branch (line ~789) checks only `typeof needle === "string"` without a `.length > 0` guard. An empty needle matches every message via String.prototype.includes("") and returns index 0 (the FIRST message). Add the same `.length > 0` guard that the by_tool_call_id and by_tool_name arms already use.

subtasks.title: Add needle.length > 0 guard in by_content_includes branch of resolveShrinkTarget

milestones.title: Rewind Tool Correctness (BUG-001, BUG-006)
milestones.description: Fix two bugs in src/tools/rewind.ts: BUG-001 (Major) — the checkpoint consumption loop clears only the first-found target when multiple targets share the same label, leaving the checkpoint active; BUG-006 (Minor) — a nuclear last_turn rewind on the first user message persists a no-op marker instead of refusing before persisting. Both are in rewindExecute but in different code regions (step 7b vs steps 5-7).

tasks.title: Fix checkpoint consumption to clear ALL matching targets (BUG-001)
tasks.description: The checkpoint-consumption loop at step 7b in rewindExecute scans getEntries() in append order, calls pi.setLabel on the FIRST matching label entry, then breaks. When two distinct targets carry the same checkpoint label (which Pi allows — labelsById is Map<targetId,label> with no cross-target uniqueness), only the oldest target is cleared. The fix: iterate ALL entries and clear EVERY target whose current getLabel matches the needle, not just the first one found.

subtasks.title: Remove break-after-first-clear; clear all targets whose getLabel matches the checkpoint needle
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/005_95d30743cdd4/bugfix/001_3f1132e1694f/architecture/bug_verification.md §BUG-001 and architecture/spec_requirements.md §BUG-001. The consumption loop at src/tools/rewind.ts lines 582-623 (step 7b) iterates getEntries() in append order, and at line 611-612 does:
  pi.setLabel(targetId, undefined);  // clears ONLY the first-found (oldest) target
  break;                             // stops — newer targets retain the label
Pi's labelsById is Map<targetId,label> with NO cross-target uniqueness. resolveCheckpoint (transforms.ts) scans branchEntries in REVERSE to find the MOST RECENT match (targetB), but the consumption loop clears targetA (oldest). After clearing targetA, checkpointExists still returns true via getLabel(targetB).
2. INPUT: The rewindExecute function in src/tools/rewind.ts, specifically the `if (granularity === "checkpoint")` block at step 7b (lines 582-623). The `needle` variable is `mulligan:checkpoint:${params.checkpoint}`. The `ctx` (ExtensionContext) provides `ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()`. The `pi` (ExtensionAPI) provides `pi.setLabel(targetId, undefined)`. The existing `checkpointExists()` function (lines 278-320) in the same file demonstrates the correct pattern: collect candidate targetIds from raw label entries, then confirm via getLabel(id) === needle.
3. LOGIC: Modify the consumption loop to clear ALL targets whose CURRENT getLabel matches the needle. Two valid approaches:
  APPROACH A (recommended — mirrors checkpointExists' pattern): After collecting candidates, iterate them and clear each whose getLabel(id) === needle. This ensures only ACTUALLY-active targets are cleared (not historical label entries that were already cleared).
  APPROACH B (simpler — clear all raw label entries matching the needle): Iterate all entries, and for each label entry matching the needle, call pi.setLabel(targetId, undefined) — WITHOUT breaking. This is simpler but may issue redundant setLabel calls for already-cleared targets (harmless — setting undefined on an already-undefined label is a no-op).
  IMPLEMENTATION (Approach A): Replace the existing loop with:
    // Collect candidate targetIds (same as checkpointExists)
    const candidates = new Set<string>();
    for (const e of entries) { ... if (ee.type === "label" && ee.label === needle && typeof ee.targetId === "string") candidates.add(ee.targetId); }
    // Clear each candidate whose CURRENT label still matches
    for (const id of candidates) { try { if (ctx.sessionManager.getLabel(id) === needle) pi.setLabel(id, undefined); } catch { /* E13 */ } }
  Keep the existing try/catch wrapping (E13: a label-clear failure must never undo the rewind — the marker is already persisted at step 7).
4. OUTPUT: The modified src/tools/rewind.ts file. After a checkpoint rewind to name "x" where two targets (targetA, targetB) both carry label "mulligan:checkpoint:x", BOTH targets are cleared. A subsequent checkpointExists(ctx, "x") returns false. A second mulligan_rewind(granularity:"checkpoint", checkpoint:"x") correctly refuses with "checkpoint 'x' not found on this branch".
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the step 7b comment block in rewind.ts to reflect the new behavior: clear ALL matching targets (not just the first found). The existing comment references 'BUG-001 fix (validation 1a)' which was a prior fix for a different sub-issue — update to note the duplicate-target fix. This rides WITH the work.

tasks.title: Refuse nuclear last_turn on first user message before persisting (BUG-006)
tasks.description: When granularity is 'last_turn' with to_previous_prompt:true and the latest user message IS the first user message, resolveLastTurn (src/transforms.ts) correctly returns {remove:[]} (protected refusal). But rewindExecute does not detect this case — it treats the empty remove as a legitimate K=0 rewind and persists a useless marker + stray note. Add an explicit protected-refusal check between resolvePreview and the persist step.

subtasks.title: Add protected-refusal check in rewindExecute for nuclear-first-user case

milestones.title: Audit Tool Consistency (BUG-005)
milestones.description: Add a config.enabled gate to mulligan_audit's auditExecute so that when the extension is disabled, the audit either reports the UNFILTERED view or refuses — rather than running filterPipeline and reporting a transformed view that does not match what the model actually sees. The rewind/shrink/cancel tools all gate on config.enabled; audit is the lone inconsistency.

tasks.title: Add config.enabled gate to mulligan_audit (BUG-005)
tasks.description: auditExecute in src/tools/audit.ts has no config.enabled check at the top. When config.enabled===false, the context handler is pass-through (model sees unfiltered context), but audit's fallback path runs filterPipeline and reports markers as active + a filtered total — actively misleading the agent about what the model sees (D5 violation). Add a config.enabled gate.

subtasks.title: Add config.enabled gate to auditExecute that reports the unfiltered view when disabled
